classification.difficultyReason: Exclude internal diameters; count concave arcs as boundary. Results are 20+8pi=45.1 cm, 10+3pi=19.4 m, 3+5.5pi=20.3 m and 30+2.625pi=38.2 km. These retained source parts use the page 54 straight-segments-plus-arcs method.

content.prompt: Calculate the perimeter of these shapes. Answer to 1 d.p.

spec.description: Convex semicircular top and concave semicircular lower boundary between equal vertical sides.
spec.mathematics: Each straight side is 10 cm; both semicircles have diameter 8 cm. The lower arc is part of the perimeter.

answer.worked:
Both semicircular arcs form part of the perimeter.
$$\begin{align*}l_{\text{top}}&=\frac12\times\pi\times8=4\pi\text{ cm}\\l_{\text{bottom}}&=4\pi\text{ cm}\\P&=10+10+4\pi+4\pi\\P&\approx45.1\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upper semicircle joined to an isosceles triangle; both dimension arrows and centre marker retained.
spec.mathematics: Diameter 6 m; both sloping sides 5 m; triangle height 4 m is retained although unnecessary for the perimeter.

answer.worked:
The dashed diameter is inside the shape.
$$\begin{align*}l&=\frac12\times\pi\times6\\l&=3\pi\text{ m}\\P&=5+5+3\pi\\P&\approx19.4\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
